answer.rationale: Write-path p99 hit 5x starting ~30m after the new release, while daily settlement peaks have been survived before. memory_b1 is the closest write-preserving fix (prior build stable, rollback without customer impact); memory_b6 supports treating a post-ship regression as release-caused. Peak load (b3) remains a live alternative, so this is not certain—b1 is the one record worth verifying because it describes an error spike, not latency. Circuit breaking risks dropping customer writes; failover and read-replica routing lack a regional or dashboard-read signal and do not clearly protect heavy settlement writes. Full rollback is required to restore availability; a tiny canary would leave most writers on the 5x path.
